question.problem:
It is known that $35%$ of the people arriving at a clothing store buy something. If the manager randomly samples $65$ customers, find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $13$ but fewer than $26$ of them bought something. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=65,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.35.$

Now, since

$$
np=65(0.35)=22.75>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=65(1-0.35)=42.25>5,
$$

and $n=65$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.35,\frac{0.35(1-0.35)}{65}) \\  & ∼N(0.35,0.0035).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If more than $13$ but fewer than $26$ people bought something, then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{13}{65}<\overset{^}{\,p} & <\frac{26}{65} \\ 0.2<\overset{^}{\,p} & <0.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(0.2\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.4).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.2\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.4) & =P(\frac{0.2-0.35}{\sqrt{0.0035}}<Z<\frac{0.4-0.35}{\sqrt{0.0035}}) \\  & ≈P(-2.54<Z<0.85) \\  & =P(Z<0.85)-P(Z<-2.54) \\  & =Φ(0.85)-Φ(-2.54)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.2\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.4) & =Φ(0.85)-Φ(-2.54).\end{aligned}
$$
